text:
Predicates:
Listed(y) ::: y is listed in Yelp’s recommendations.
ReceivesManyNegativeReviews(y) ::: y receives many negative reviews.
RatingGreaterThan9(y) ::: y has a rating greater than 9.
ProvidesTakeOut(y) ::: y provides take-out service.
PopularAmongLocals(y) ::: y is popular among local residents.
Subway ::: the restaurant Subway.
Premises:
∀y (Listed(y) → ¬ReceivesManyNegativeReviews(y)) ::: If a restaurant is listed in Yelp’s recommendations, then it does not receive many negative reviews.
∀y (RatingGreaterThan9(y) → Listed(y)) ::: All restaurants with a rating greater than 9 are listed in Yelp’s recommendations.
∃y (¬ProvidesTakeOut(y) ∧ ReceivesManyNegativeReviews(y)) ::: Some restaurants that do not provide take-out service receive many negative reviews.
∀y (PopularAmongLocals(y) → RatingGreaterThan9(y)) ::: All restaurants that are popular among local residents have ratings greater than 9.
RatingGreaterThan9(Subway) ∨ PopularAmongLocals(Subway) ::: Subway has a rating greater than 9 or is popular among local residents.
Conclusion:
ProvidesTakeOut(Subway) ∧ ReceivesManyNegativeReviews(Subway) → (RatingGreaterThan9(Subway) ∧ ¬ProvidesTakeOut(Subway))
